subject: ing
title: Spanish verb times: one word or two?

points.heading: One-word verb times
points.body:
A **verb** names an action. To **conjugate** means to change it for who speaks and for **when** it happens. In the indicative mood we tell facts as real stories, not wishes. With **cantar** (to sing): **canto** is now, **cantaba** is a past that keeps going, **canté** is a closed past, **cantaré** is later, **cantaría** is «would.» The **stem** is cant-; the **ending** finishes the word. Those five forms are all **one word** each. Practice: Your turn. Write canto, cantaba, canté, cantaré, and cantaría with yo. Say what time each one points to.

Look at a real case of "One-word verb times". Say one sentence about what you learned.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Práctica: Ahora te toca a ti.

Common mistake: Error común:

points.heading: Two-word verb times
points.body:
Sometimes Spanish uses **two words**: a form of **haber** (he, has, ha…) plus the **participle**, the already-done form ending in -ado or -ido. Here **haber** is a helper, not «there is.»

**He cantado** means the singing already happened and still matters now. **Había comido** means someone had already eaten before another past moment. The participle stays the same for he, she, or we—it does not gain -s for plural.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Your turn. Write he cantado and había comido. Underline the participle in each pair.

Common mistake: Say hemos comido, not hemos comidos.

points.heading: One word or two?
points.body:
Choose by **when** and whether the result still matters. **Ayer terminé** uses one word because yesterday closed the action. **Ya he terminado** uses two because the result is still alive now.

**Leía** when **sonó** the phone mixes background (one word) with a sudden closed hit (another one word). Time words like ayer, ya, and cuando are clues—not rules you can ignore.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Your turn. Write one sentence with one verb word and one with two verb words about your week.

Common mistake: With a closed «yesterday,» do not force «ayer he ido.»

lesson.summary: Learn to narrate **when** something happens: one-word verb forms or two-word forms (haber + participle), choosing with meaning.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).
